item.title: Friendship bracelet seeking greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An anomalous bracelet which removes the wearers ability to experience any and all negative emotions. This bracelet then compels its wearer to create "friendship bracelets" out of available materials and attempts to convince others to wear these bracelets. the original bracelet changes size in order to always fit its wearer, the other bracelets created by an affected person have all the same effects excluding this one.

Central Narrative: The story will be told through an interview log of an agent who was sent as part of a pair to investigate a quickly growing cult. The cult was in possession of the original bracelet and all of its members were wearing other instances. The agent will have been tortured, along with their partner dying to the torture, and was recovered along with the SCP when an MTF was deployed.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The story is an exploration of the implications of a person (or group of people) having a single goal that consumes their life. This exploration is diversified by the individuals not having negative emotions (which lead to morals) to "hold them back".

Additional Notes: I have a draft of the SCP article, and would like tweaks before I write the interview.

Sometimes The Foundation is content if the SCP disappears into the woodwork, and in this case, they may be willing to accept the loss if it gets rid of him, especially if they have a general idea where he is.

item.title: Re: Two SCP green light
item.content:encoded:
1) The containment is a no-brainer: If they both have humanoid forms then just set a room up for them to nuzzle in. That puts him and his nullification abilities in the center of a site with no problems. After all, if he does whatever she says and she can be convinced to come in willingly, it would be easy.

I'd also point out that "containment" doesn't mean "onsite". A number of SCPs are contained without forcing them into an actual site or even penned up. "Containment" is all about neutralizing the threat, and if that means just ensuring that the SCP has a wide berth, then so be it; whichever way is expeditious is the way The Foundation usually goes.

Strictly as a side note, I'd point out that a number of SCPs fall in the same category of invulnerability; if the dragon really is a Keter-level threat (and he sounds like it), then he can be dealt with either directly or by sending him to another dimension.

2) The monstrous forms are the problem here, just because of its two gigantic monstrous forms. However, if you point out that they prefer humanoid form then there shouldn't be a problem. The humanoid forms would also take out caspian's problem.

3) A better hook is "love will find a way". The cool part here is that you have two different forms of immortality (long-term versus a cycle of death/renewal) and that they need to find a way to make their romance work. In the messed-up world of The Foundation, THAT is much cooler than just worrying about some relatively trivial containment issue.

4) As long as the two are a pair, this is technically ONE SCP (XXXX-1/XXXX-2). Just sayin'….

item.title: Re: Two SCP green light
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Dr Poss. Let's take a look at your concept.

So this was… an interesting read. Hahaha. I'm not sure what it says about me that I was trying to picture how exactly a dragon and a phoenix would "mate" with each other. My first advice to you would be remove the dragon aspect and replace it with just another male phoenix. Why overcomplicate the anomaly? We call this stretching the imagination beyond belief, and unless you already have some established fantasy world like Tolkien's Lord of the Rings, having BOTH dragons and phoenixes in the same world is slightly pushing it. Of course, if you feel strongly there's a reason to include both, please let me know below.

My second concern are the themes you seem to be advocating through the narrative. The "Dragon" figure comes across as too controlling and slightly abusive one in the relationship. I'm guessing that's what you were going for, and plan on frowning upon in the article? I do like the fact that the female phoenix keeps forgetting him, but the two end up falling in love each time again, aka Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind (do check it out).

His raw power making containment of him or her near impossible.

My last concern is with regards to this line - so what is the Foundation's involvement in your storyline? How do we go about containing both entities? The majority of your pitch is spent detailing both the dragon and phoenix. But that doesn't tell us what the rest of your article will read like. Will there exploration logs? testing logs? Basically, what does the Foundation do upon discovering these two?

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I'll try to take another look. For now, all the best!

item.title: Re: Utensils waiting for greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Dr Sharpless. Let's take a look at your concept.

So my main issue seems to be trying to connect all the features you've listed throughout the pitch. How do spoons, forks and other utensils link to an Italian man, a spinning effect and the abilities to incapacitate people (or turn them into midgets) who come near? Do you see that your list of anomalous traits are seemingly completely random?

Ideally, keep your anomaly simple and sweet. I'd advise new authors to stick to one (or two max) anomalous properties, and more importantly, come up with a plausible explanation for their existence. I don't see any of that detail in the current pitch. Is the Italian dude a spoon-maker, for example? Did he curse the utensils for some reason? Why are the spoons spinning? Are they being controlled by the spirit of the Italian man?

If you decide to revise your concept, do drop me another PM and I'll try to take another look. For now, all the best!

item.title: Re: The No-Tell Motel
item.content:encoded:
Hi Gryphon Watcher, thank you for your elaboration.

It's origins are unknown, and if the staff know they are refusing to answer, but it's goal seems to be to draw in "guests", in some cases with an intent to give them anomalous properties/abilities.

Hmm. This is still the part that's problematic for me. You've described A LOT of various anomalous properties that the hotel manifests, and I get that it's a place of intersecting universes, so this kind of randomness is to be expected.

But you need to have an explanation for the base anomaly. What exactly are its origins, and why does it want to draw guests in and turn them into anomalies themselves. I feel that if you were to explore this strand further, this will be your Central Narrative and the basis of your breaching and exploration logs. The Foundation has to investigate the anomaly and ultimately reach a conclusion of sorts. What is this conclusion?

Right now, the description sounds very cool, but it also sounds like an episode of Interdimensional Cable from Rick & Morty (you should check it out). While it's cool for a while to see random things happening, there has to be an underlying narrative that ties things together. Otherwise, it's just a series of random occurences and there's no payoff.

For what it's worth, I think you're on the right track, and you're close to a greenlight from me. Continue expanding on what the end goal of the article will look like?

item.title: Typowriter (Seeking Greenlight/Critiques or Edits)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Highly powerful reality bender manifesting in the form of a common typewriter. The typewriter will essentially create "transcripts" of nearby media, although it often makes typos. If a typo happens to create a sentence in the transcript that grammatically makes sense, it will become reality. It runs forever and will make increasingly more typos on a transcript if the same piece of media is shown to it multiple times.

Central Narrative: I plan for this to be an SCP that has been in containment for awhile, however without any reliable containment procedures. There will be an extensive list of research notes and observations about the operations of SCP XXXX. The main "narrative" stems from a recovered journal. The SCP is contained by singing up 4 unwitting rural towns to use their local news stations, newspapers, and radio broadcasts for SCP XXXX. Although MTFs patrol all 4 towns constantly, one woman begins to keep a journal of all the weird alterations that happen, so she can be sure she isn't going crazy (as the towns are frequently amnestizied due to the SCP)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Completely random reality bender that is able to warp anything by writing a typo

Additional Notes: The reality anchors do not work on this SCP, in actuality because it kills some of the fun associated with it. I think a decent theory within the narrative as to why this is so is that SCP XXXX is a recovered byproduct of SCP 3812 (SCP-3812)

item.title: Greenlight Concept - Article - Horror/History -Related to Sarkicism & CotBG
item.content:encoded:
Seeking review of concept for an SCP article. Tried this out about nine years ago, did bad, and want to give it another go having read a lot more of the material and matured as a writer/person.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror & History

Page Layout (Optional): Standard in-depth containment procedure, followed by a retrieval log and accompanied by a brief test log with two or three addenda related to the nature of the SCP. I don't want to perform anything out of the ordinary format-wise with it being my first entry, but a timeline of the SCP's apprehension by groups of interest may be relevant.

Elevator Pitch:

A forest-spirit/lesser goddess of creation and fertility that asexually births creatures based
upon what she consumes is captured by the Church of the Broken God, and turned into a weapon to convert organic material into inorganic material. They lose her, and she exchanges hands between organizations for hundreds of years before ending up in foundation custody totally unrecognizable to what she once was, with a sinister corruption of her godly ability.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:

Following the first war of the Flesh, Cyrus the Great founded a covenant to search the world for a new means to defeat the Sarkic threat. This group set out, with generations passing before eventually finding a minor fertility goddess unique in her ability to produce life asexually and rapidly by consuming organic matter. They captured her, but became indoctrinated by the Church of the Broken God over time, and augmented her heavily. She would eventually escape with the aid of a man enamored with her, and sire a child with him, the location of which is unknown but she is believed to be endowed with the same ability. Over time different organizations got ahold of the spirit and altered her repeatedly to suit their needs or designs with her now bordering on unrecognizable as herself.

Her modern iteration is a mess of added mechanical and organic apertures both internal and external that have removed her god-like beauty to some extent. Her mistreatment by mankind has jaded her to the point of being predatory, and resulted in her fractured psyche turning to exploitation and predation of mankind through producing her unique offspring. Organic material she consumed is now converted into mechanically augmented horrors when she births them, and vice versa.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

The concept of the perversion of sexuality, creation, and birth for the purpose of furthering an agenda is enticing and provocative. Taking an earthly minor-goddess of creation and weaponizing her between the Sarkites and Mekhanites and turning her into a cog in the war machine between them serves as a potent analogy for the corruption of life and nature to fit the destruction of it, while sympathizing the reader to a malignant goddess that was once benign and pure.

Additional Notes: I believe I've thought this through reasonably well, but am making space to afford the word count. Some gaps in reasoning are apparent here that I don't have space to explain.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Greenlight Concept - Article - Horror / History -Related to Sarkicism & CotBG

item.title: Re: Greenlight time?
item.content:encoded:
Awesome, thank you for the quick reply!
I think I can keep this an interesting SCP proper, given some nice hefty changes. How do these changes sound:

1. Yes, on reflection I think there's no reason the Serpent's Hand needs to get involved (maybe they'll take an interest in a tale or somethin, or that interaction will just stay in my own headcanon).

2. However, I think the Chaos Insurgency still fits pretty well, and "Coyote" would definitely gravitate to them over the Foundation. But perhaps this turn of events works best as the final note?

3. Time to simplify the plot. Remove SH involvement, and go into less detail about the anthropologist character and how the Foundation discovered the SCP.

4. However, I'm not sure whether to remove the Foundation's attempted first contact (If I do keep it, I think I can rework it to make their method more interesting). If I keep it, it can open the storytelling opportunity for the next "file" to be a report of Coyote's betrayal and realignment with the CI. But of course, just cutting all that out would majorly simplify things.

Basically, I'm not sure whether it's acceptable for the most recent development to be Coyote "joining" the CI (and therefore being currently uncontained). Or perhaps the Foundation just throws resources at it via cultural suppression and weaken him so much that he stops being a problem (or so they think). That second ending might warrant an Ethics Committee log.

How do those changes and proposals sound?
Thank you, I really appreciate the feedback, I do want to make a good article.

item.title: Re: What is your favourite SCP?
item.content:encoded:
I really have to put another vote in here for SCP-3999. That SCP single-handedly convinced me that there's something special going on here on the wiki, and that I wanted to be part of it.

It's strange too, because it's one of the few SCPs where the particulars don't really matter. You could cut a lot from or add a lot of stuff to the first half, and it wouldn't change much. It's not some masterclass in carefully crafting the perfect word-by-word story. Yet, it has had more of an effect on how I consume fiction than any other piece of fiction.

I read it at first, and honestly tried my hardest to hate it. I tried to think that it was pretentious nonsense. But, eventually…

SCP-3999 won.

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: A child discovers he can make living shadow puppets on walls with a light source and his hands. Unfortunately, he doesn't know how to completely control them. Ends with implications that the Foundation may use him as a weapon.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: A child is playing under a blanket fort with his parents. After his father shows him how to make shadow puppets with a flashlight and his hands, the child follows suit. The shadows he makes are living, and proceed to "devour" his parents. After not seeing the family leave their house for a while, police are called to the scene. After they enter, gunshots are heard, and then shadows dart around the house. A junior researcher who lives nearby calls in the situation and Foundation agents contain the child. The junior researcher is assigned to the SCP and tries to calm him down, though he knows what the Foundation might do to the child.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The story of an innocent child doing normal things that becomes under the control of the cold and calculating Foundation.

item.title: Re: SCP idea: Retroactive weight gain supplement
item.content:encoded:
Let's see what we have here.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

you start to gain memories from before you were born of being something not human.

This part seems to appear out of the blue. Like, you have all these properties about weight loss and then you mention this. What does this have to do with the rest of the concept? I mean, you can add a depth meaning to the pills thing, but you need to have some kind of build-up, not just making it to appear spontaneously.

That said, I think some kind of twist like that would be interesting. The anomaly itself is pretty basic, and I think something like this would help a lot to improve it. What are these "new memories" about? What's the meaning of these memories? Maybe some kind of being wanted us to remember them? Maybe that being created the pills in order to attract us by using a common human desire? If you focus on this part, I think your article would be very interesting.

I haven't decided yet how much it affects other people's memories

I think other people's memories would be unaffected. Like, maybe they just don't want to hurt the subject's feelings? Maybe the subject's in denial about what others say? This is a common effect of real eating disorders, so it would make this concept to feel somewhat realistic.

or physical records like pictures.

Like I said, maybe they're just in denial of these records? Or maybe they see the records in a different manner?

I haven't decided yet what happens if you stop taking the pills, though it probably depends on if you have passed the critical point or not.

Maybe if they stop eating the pills, the memories slowly start to get back to normal? Maybe they forget about eating the pills in the first place? Maybe they start to have some kind of side effects? Perhaps the pills are like a drug?

Overall, I think that you should add some kind of backstory to the existence of the pills.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look.

item.title: Re: “Anti foundation” SCP
item.content:encoded:
You've got two basic problems:

1) What exactly is the goal of the "anti-foundations"? Are they trying to destroy The Foundation from within, steal SCPs, steal information, and/or slow it down? If they just worship the deity and only hate The Foundation, that's not in and of itself enough to create an MTF to take the people out. The most likely event is that they would tag the personnel involved and round them up, keeping them under control until they can figure out what's going on.

If they've all been marked MIA, it's likely that they would be found out during debriefing, something that The Foundation does a thorough job of considering that they deal with shapeshifters, possessors, and other infiltrators. Someone who was marked as MIA but came back would be seen as very suspicious under The Foundation's circumstances, and so the debriefing would be very thorough. As such, they would likely be caught by agents with no need for an MTF.

Unless, of course, they gained some sort of combat enhancement through their experience…

2) There either is an entity of some sort or there isn't. Since there is an effect, there has to be an entity of some sort. As such you need to actually define it. The fewer the mysteries the better, and if it's just a mystery for the sake of a mystery, that won't cut it.

Let's see what we have here.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

he ends up risking up the veil and getting the community he so much loved killed

What happened? What did he do? I'm guessing it has something to do with the memetic agent. Did they all start to feel the 'bad' effects? Did he try to improve the feelings of his music? Also, why did he get persecuted? You're being very ambiguous with this part; I think you should explain this a little more in order to understand the exact things that happened.

he releases the memetic agent with ambiguous motivations.

Why did he release it? What was he thinking? Was he sad, angry, impulsive…? I don't see any motive to release the agent on a global scale. I think you should explain his motives in your concept post; even if they're going to be ambiguous in the article, you should have them clear in your mind.

is it really better to live on your knees than to die on your feet?

What? When did that dilemma come to be? Why is it a part of the story? It seems to appear out of the blue, and I don't see any connection with the story about a guy trying to improve his music. How are you going to portray this in your article?

Is the Foundation really willing to declare a war on artistic expression for the greater good?

What? What happened in order for the Foundation to declare open war on something? Did the agent get out of control? What happened to the world? You didn't say anything about this part in your concept.

Overall, I think your concept is missing some key points regarding the story you're planning to tell.

item.title: Re: seeking greenlights: a forest clearing
item.content:encoded:
Let's see what we have here.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

The pocket dimension is something like a paradise version of the original forest clearing

I think you should explain a little more on this. What do you mean by 'paradise'? What's different from the real forest? You can play with the descriptions and/or physics of the pocket dimension. I think you should try to make the reader into 'feel' the sensation of what is like to be there.

in the middle of the forest clearing is an old ruin

Who lived there? Why no one lives there anymore? You can play with this. What was life like in there? You can have a lot of worldbuilding here. Maybe you can use it to show how a civilization living in "paradise" rose and fell? Maybe you can make this a metaphor of utopias and their inevitable collapse?

the portal got unstable and is now neutralized

This part could also be a metaphor about "dream places" being destined to collapse. This would be a nice and simple ending to a good story.

the will to stay in the pd grows with the time

Maybe, along with the pd, the traces of the civilization also grow? This way your story will have some type of escalation through the article. Maybe you could write one exploration log about a D-Class going in there and being happy while discovering the place's history?

if anyone tries to force someone to exit the pd after they spent more than 13 min in it, they'll do everything just to stay there

So how did the person who got lost even get out? I think they would've never leave, just because they would've not feel the necessity to do so. I think you should either get rid of this property, or came up with another story regarding its discovery. Maybe some disappearances? Maybe a group of friends find it and one of them got inside and didn't want to exit?

Overall, you have the opportunity to do a lot of worldbuilding here, and I think that would improve your article.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look.
